extracted.intended_audience: Title IX Coordinators; administrators and compliance officers at LEAs (local educational agencies), IHEs (institutions of higher education), and other recipients of federal education funds
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of compliance requirements, procedural expectations, and administrative burdens imposed by the Department's Title IX final regulations, focused on supportive measures, investigations/adjudications, appeals, informal resolution, recordkeeping, monitoring, and training. Applicable to LEAs, IHEs, and other recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for Title IX Coordinators
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide training for Title IX Coordinators; the Department estimates additional hours in Year 1 and ongoing years and assumes recipients will update and possibly develop more comprehensive training materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates: 2 additional hours per Title IX Coordinator in Year 1 and 1 hour in future years; one-time centralized training development cost may occur (Department estimated a one-time cost of $9,548,382 for training development). Materials may be developed in a variety of ways; some entities may develop materials to be used across many recipients. The Department did not receive supplementary data to revise estimates further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures in response to information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to offer supportive measures, as appropriate, to complainants and respondents in response to information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment and prohibited retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement expands beyond the 2020 amendments' 'actual knowledge' trigger. For sex-based harassment and prohibited retaliation, supportive measures are expected to be similar and usually will not create additional measurable cost. The Department cannot prescribe specific measures due to case-by-case variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to alter alleged conduct to provide supportive measures for non-harassment sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: For allegations of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment or prohibited retaliation, recipients are not required to alter the conduct that is alleged to be sex discrimination for the purpose of providing a supportive measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department expects little impact on costs from this provision. Information about unequal access to resources/facilities or individualized differential treatment typically leads to measures such as eliminating the source of discrimination (e.g., improving facilities) or academic adjustments (e.g., allowing student to attend different section). Additional costs may arise from addressing the underlying discrimination (not classified as supportive-measure costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and expected costs of commonly-provided supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures vary widely and must be tailored to the situation; the Department used common measures to estimate costs and added a flat cost per incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: facility improvements, academic adjustments (changing class section or instructor), counseling. Department assumption: many measures are already provided and per-incident costs are de minimis, but a flat additional cost of $250 per incident was used for modeling. Time assumptions: at LEAs — 2 hours Title IX Coordinator + 2 hours administrative assistant; at IHEs/other — 2 hours Title IX Coordinator + 1 hour administrative assistant. Average per-incident cost estimates derived (e.g., ~$565 per incident at LEAs, ~$504 at IHEs/others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling assumptions for supportive measures (incident increases and acceptance rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department assumes an increase in the number of incidents prompting offers of supportive measures and an acceptance rate to estimate total burden/costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions: final regulations will double (100% increase) the incidents prompting offers compared to investigations under 2020 amendments; recipients assume supportive measures are accepted in approximately 90% of incidents in which they are offered. Specific per-recipient provision estimates: LEAs provide supportive measures ~6.40 times/year (assumed 90% acceptance), IHEs 11.29 times/year, other recipients 3.96 times/year. These modeling assumptions drive the Department's aggregate cost estimates (e.g., net increase of $9,142,455/year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Title IX coverage for investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.11 clarifies Title IX applies to every recipient and all prohibited sex discrimination occurring under a recipient's education program or activity, including when some contributing conduct occurred outside the recipient's program or outside the United States, so long as it contributed to a sex-based hostile environment under the recipient's program/activity in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not obligated under Title IX to receive/process complaints about conduct occurring outside the United States unless it is alleged to have contributed to a domestic hostile environment. Investigations of incidents with out-of-country conduct may be more time-consuming, but costs for investigating conduct wholly outside the United States need not be borne under the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations and adjudications procedural and time-burden expectations by recipient group
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department uses a three-group framework (Group A, B, C) to estimate likely recipient responses and associated time burdens for investigations and adjudications, specifying hours per role (Title IX Coordinator, administrative assistant, lawyers/advisors, investigators, adjudicators) under baseline (2020) and final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of Department assumptions (selected): Group A LEA baseline investigation: 3 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 4 hrs admin assistant, 6 hrs investigator, 2 hrs adjudicator, lawyers/advisors involved in ~15% of cases (2 hrs each). Under final regs Group A LEA: 4 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 2 hrs admin assistant. IHEs and 'other' recipients have different hour assumptions; Department also assumes flat $100 adjudication recording cost when present. These time allocations are used to compute per-recipient and aggregate cost estimates (detailed tables provided in the document).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording/transcript requirements for hearings and certain meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: IHEs may hold live hearings but are not required to; when a live hearing is conducted, the IHE must create an audio or audiovisual recording, or transcript, and make it available for inspection and review. Postsecondary institutions must create a recording or transcript of individual meetings with a party or witness conducted to satisfy §106.46(f)(1)(i)(A), even if no live hearing is held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department accounted for recording/transcript costs in estimates. Assumed flat recording rates: $100 per adjudication for many recipients (IHEs sometimes $200 where transcripts/official records expected). Under final regulations, assumed no change in the flat rate for IHEs/other recipients where recording occurs; LEAs assumed to have few recording costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer appeals of dismissals and parity of appeal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: All recipients must offer an appeal of a dismissal of a sex discrimination complaint; the final regulations expand this obligation to dismissals of any sex discrimination complaint, not just sex-based harassment dismissals. Additionally, recipients must offer parties an appeal process that is at least the same as in comparable proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IHEs must continue to offer an appeal process for sex-based harassment complaints involving a student party; LEAs and other recipients are no longer required to offer appeals for determinations in a sex-based harassment complaint but must offer appeals of dismissals. Modeling assumptions: ~50% of fully adjudicated complaints have one or more parties appeal. Department assumed specific time burdens per role for appeals (e.g., LEA appeal: 2 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 2 hrs admin assistant, 2 hrs each for two lawyers/advisors, 6 hrs adjudicator) and estimated aggregate cost increase from additional appeals (~$17,776,304/year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution process expectations and burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer informal resolution; the final regulations are expected to have de minimis effect on the proportion of complaints resolved informally and not materially change burden per informal resolution, though informal resolution may require more Title IX Coordinator and administrative assistant time than an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The elimination of the formal complaint precondition may leave most complainants' propensity to choose informal resolution unchanged. Department assumed additional burdens if informal resolution is used: LEAs — +1 hr Title IX Coordinator and +5 hrs admin assistant above investigation/adjudication baseline; IHEs — +2.5 hrs Title IX Coordinator and +1 hr admin assistant; other recipients — +1 hr Title IX Coordinator and +3 hrs admin assistant. Informal resolution assumed to eliminate costs for investigators, adjudicators, recording, and lawyers/advisors at LEAs and other recipients (but IHEs might still involve lawyers/advisors: assumed 6 hrs each for two lawyers/advisors). Department estimated increased cost from additional informal resolutions (~$14,068,164/year) based on anticipated increases in complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping expansion and system modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.8(f) broadens recordkeeping requirements to apply to all notifications to the Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and all complaints of sex discrimination; recipients must modify recordkeeping systems accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients that already maintain broader records under state/local requirements may see no additional burden; recipients that only maintained records related to sexual harassment will see increased burden. Department estimated Year 1 modification time: LEAs — 2 hrs each for Title IX Coordinator and admin assistant; IHEs — 4 hrs Title IX Coordinator, 8 hrs admin assistant, 4 hrs database administrator ($77.54/hr); other recipients — 2 hrs each for Title IX Coordinator and admin assistant. Ongoing yearly increases also estimated (e.g., ongoing increase ~$5,237,728/year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for barriers to reporting and required responsive steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure their Title IX Coordinator monitors the education program or activity for barriers to reporting conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and take steps reasonably calculated to address such barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department expects many recipients, especially IHEs, already monitor for barriers to reduce liability. Some recipients may create new low-cost monitoring mechanisms: incorporate barrier-related questions into training materials, include questions in conversations with students/employees, conduct roundtable discussions or listening sessions. The Department assumes Title IX Coordinators are motivated to proactively identify and address barriers; many actions chosen will have de minimis costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of incidents previously handled in alternative disciplinary processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the 2020 amendments many recipients shifted incidents outside §106.45 into alternative disciplinary processes; the Department assumes resource/time expenditures for these alternative processes mirror student conduct or previous grievance processes and that, under the final regulations, incidents previously handled outside Title IX grievance procedures will be handled under Title IX grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department provides time-burden assumptions for alternative processes (examples: LEA alternative process requires 3 hrs administrator, 14 hrs admin assistant, 6 hrs each for two lawyers/advisors in 5% of cases, 6 hrs investigator; IHE alternative process: 6 hrs administrator, 20 hrs admin assistant, 10 hrs each for two lawyers/advisors, 15 hrs investigator). Under final regs, many incidents will revert to Title IX grievance process, with different hour assumptions detailed in Group B tables, producing net changes in aggregate costs (e.g., Group B net decrease of ~$63,650,843/year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibilities to tailor grievance procedures to educational settings
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations include flexibilities allowing recipients to develop grievance procedures tailored to their educational settings to reduce burden per complaint while ensuring fair investigations and adjudications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes exercise of flexibilities will not impair fairness but will allow recipients to avoid requirements that previously forced use of specialized individuals (e.g., supplemental specialized investigators for LEAs). Examples: reducing per-case specialized personnel use, modifying time allocations per role as reflected in Group A assumptions under final regs. These flexibilities inform the Department's assumption that per-complaint burdens may decrease even as complaint counts increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions about involvement rates and flat fees for legal/adjudicative activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For modeling, the Department assumes specific percentages for when lawyers/advisors are involved and applies flat fees for recording or transcripts where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lawyers/advisors involved in ~15% of investigations in many settings (Group A), 5% in some alternative processes, two lawyers/advisors assumed when present; flat recording rates assumed: typically $100 per adjudication, $200 for some IHE hearings where transcripts/official records may be desired. These assumptions are used to calculate aggregate cost estimates; commenters did not provide data to modify them.
